notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
No updates were released this month, but the game's soundtrack has been fully uploaded to the channel, and some progress was made!
[h1]Crafting manual[/h1]
[list]
Due to the lack of information in the early game relating to crafting recipes, a crafting manual will be in the next update, allowing players to see all the crafting recipes in the game, and unobtained items are blacked out!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/334b0c67296b3d384625b7e0deceeb6aac1a5658.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h1]Sunset colors[/h1]
[list]
Now for a graphical change. Sunsets and sunrises will glow with a red-orange tinge before going dark in the next update!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/62834a921069ba43c38f67072edbc3ccfff337c6.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h1]New shield stat: Hazard[/h1]
[list]
Shields also have a new addition: Hazards. This new stat blocks damage from environmental hazards, such as lava, poison, cactus floors, and hazards like it, although it doesn't block status effect damage!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/86ed64926281274b7c015e75ed55f1421b9a1e2d.png[/img]
(Hazard icon indicated by the spike icon)
[/list]
[h1]Technical changes[/h1]
[list]
Most of these new changes were done in the first half of the month, but I've mostly been focusing on the technical side lately, especially the enemy code.

Due to the game's enemy codebase, it's often a complicated process to add an enemy to the game, and the enemy codebase is now being rebuilt nearly from the ground up to be more flexible than the current one. This is where most of the effort's being concentrated at the moment.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
With these changes, alongside plans to scrap planetary exploration in favor of asteroid mining, and porting Aquatica's content to Tierra in the form of oceans, it's likely that the next update will be months away, and development will be somewhat slow for the foreseeable future, but I will get there eventually!

It's expected that the remainder of the tracks will be uploaded on the YouTube channel sometime next month at this rate!

[h1]Technical implementation of shields (Math involved!)[/h1]
[list]
When a player gets damaged, a variable, which I'll call [damage multiplier], is calculated with this formula below, with [i]m[/i] as a constant, and [i]x[/i] is the total armor of the player:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/15422684859aa89fe1a95084cfb0829a9ddc7f64.png[/img]
[damage multiplier] will always be a value between 0 and 1, and the armor always has a minimum value of 0. Once [damage multiplier] is calculated, the damage taken by the player is multiplied by [damage multiplier].
E.g. The player gets 80 damage, and has 50 armor. [damage multiplier] is calculated to be 0.571, whose product is 45.71. Its rounded up to 46, and the player receives 46 damage as a result.

Here's a graph displaying the relationship between [damage multiplier] and armor:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/eb86f94dd034c0dd6436b54089e9fe977e601647.png[/img]

[h1]A potentially radical direction change...[/h1]
[list]
[h2]Lack of direction[/h2]
[list]
Due to a lack of direction for what the future of Cosmorists should be apart from adding random content here and there, where it was this way for quite a while now, I highly considered changing the direction of the game to cut back on ambition, while also staying true to the game's space theme.
[/list]
[h2]Cut out Luna, Move Aquatica's content to Tierra[/h2]
[list]
Although planetary exploration has existed in the game for around 2 years now, due to slow progress and lack of motivation lately, and especially lack of direction on what to do next, I've considered cutting out planetary exploration entirely, such as cutting out Luna, only preserving it for existing saves to maintain backwards compatibility.

At the same time, Aquatica is also cut out as its own planet, but all of its content is moved to Tierra where in a future update, Tierra would generate oceans across the surface alongside a new beach biome bordering oceans, and if the player walks into an ocean, it transitions to an ocean frontier resembling Aquatica, with walls generating where the land is, and if a player touches those walls, it'll take the player back to the surface.

In cave systems, I also envision unbreakable walls separating oceans from Tierra's current cave biomes, so players don't walk into an underwater biome, and get crushed by the water pressure, where the deepest that underwater biomes can go would be roughly layer 500 until going back to lava caves.
[/list]
[h2]More distinct resource identities[/h2]
[list]
The thing that will likely be a high priority at the moment is to give each resource a more distinct identity. Shields are already undergoing another change shortly after the On the Defense update:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/ecc105dd94a8b04e27d7d93fea6dfcf0c92903f1.png[/img]

In the above screenshot, instead of each shield having a general armor stat that blocks nearly all types of damage, each shield will block different types of damage, blocking one type of damage very well but offering weak protection in others. So far, it's melee, projectile, and blast armor, but I'm considering adding a 4th one, one for hazards, a stat that blocks damage from cactus floors in desert caves, poison in jungle/wilting caves, or lava in lava caves, anything static that damages the player on contact!

In the screenshot shown, copper shields will be great for early defense against melee attacks, but will offer little protection against explosions or projectiles (stats are subject to change).

Tin shields are strong at blocking projectile damage, but less so with melee or explosive damage. 

Iron shields will offer the best protection against explosions, but blocks slightly less melee damage than copper shields, and slightly less projectile damage than tin shields, but has higher durability, and so on.

Another change made is that copper swords and tin arrows will now deal 50% more damage, and tin bows will shoot arrows around 40% farther.

This rebalance is primarily to give existing resources more contrast with others, and a stronger sense of identity instead of rare metals having strictly better stats than metals before it. In the early game combat space, copper tools will now be best for melee combat, and tin is best for ranged combat. For the shields, it still uses that same formula as described in the technical implementation, but now applied to different damage types!

Beyond just combat, I have plenty of ideas on where to take this, something like a gadget giving +20% movement speed but only in a specific biome found in that biome's treasure or a rare enemy drop, or a gadget that gives the player immunity to a certain debuff, or a set of 2 or 3 shields in the shields slot giving the player something like +10% melee damage or +25% movement speed when damaged, the ideas can go on and on!
[/list]
[h2]Asteroid exploration direction[/h2]
[list]
Alongside this planetary exploration cut, the spaceship will still exist, and the large biome and landing site system will also still be around, but instead of exploring other planets, I considered replacing it with some kind of explorable asteroid field around Tierra to keep the game's space exploration theme.

In this asteroid field, the spaceship is stationary, and the cosmorist can leave the spaceship tethered to it for oxygen to mine asteroids for ore and other resources, with hostile alien spaceships serving as enemies. The more distant from Tierra the spaceship is, the more valuable asteroids there will be, but also the more dangerous the hostile spaceships get.

Here's roughly what I envision the asteroid field to look like:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/1f9ff287f9871f21d68ac0e5e7b5010cc865d0e4.gif[/img]

If I do go through, this will likely be a low priority thing at first due to the focus on resource functionality.
[/list]
[h2]Automation serving as endgame content[/h2]
[list]
After early ambitions for automation once it was added into the game over a year ago, only to not add much to it since then, in this direction change, automation content will likely still be added, but serve primarily as end-game content instead of mid-game content, as the game's foundations were more focused on being a survival-crafting sandbox game instead of an automation game.
[/list]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
Now that we're halfway into 2025 (time flies!), this new direction and cuts on planetary exploration content may be a rough choice for me to make, but this pivot is primarily to prevent scope creep from getting too out of hand and slowing me down, and for Cosmorists not to be stuck in early access for multiple years longer than it should.
This is also to ensure content that does get added is concentrated on one planet instead of being spread thin across multiple planets!

notes.title: v 0.1.5 - On the defensive!
notes.content:
Another month has passed since the last update, this time, the update brings a sense of defense to the game alongside other content!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/886b109a5bb2d6d6876d33b94b635ff362b285e2.png[/img]
[h1]Shields![/h1]
[list]
[*] An update with "defensive" in the name certainly has something to do with defense. Introducing shields!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/55d516dc8e4eb1492ad2ff02b7e56ceef5627f9c.png[/img]
With this update also come new inventory slots dedicated to shields. The number on the top left is a new stat: Armor! It determines how much damage is blocked by something physical, such as direct enemy damage or a projectile, and has no effect on damage taken by status effects such as Burning or Poison. (Note, Stone shields have 5 armor and 504 durability after a rebalance instead of 8 and 630 as seen in the screenshot)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/21a0515a12bcb0817e2ae7284b25f13d4106c555.png[/img]
There are also several different types of shields as well for each ore, each giving varying amounts of armor to the player, and different durability amounts, and if an enemy damages the player, the shield absorbs some of it!

[h3]Functionality[/h3]
[list]
The new shield system computes damage in a proportional manner. The higher the armor stat, the less damage the player takes, but proportional. At 62 armor, the player will take roughly half as much damage as a player at 0 armor, so if an enemy deals 50 damage, the player will take 25 damage.

The amount of durability lost from damage can also vary depending on inflicted damage and armor, usually below, but close to the inflicted damage.
[/list]
[/list]

[h1]Major enemy rebalance![/h1]
[list]
Alongside the new shields, the amount of damage that mid to high tier enemies deal is now much higher to go alongside the new shields, sometimes double or even triple their original damage apart from lower tier ones such as the Plain Slime.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/585fee665a907deb9309d9f75df676534df25f79.gif[/img]
Here's the revamped damage of a Large Molten Slime for instance. It has the same AI as before, but now able to one-shot any unshielded cosmorist, even at full health!
[/list]

[h1]Spaceship weight rebalance![/h1]
[list]
Due to spaceships being fairly restrictive in most cases with the weight system in what players can bring, players are now able to carry 10x more weight on their spaceships, while still applying some pressure for players to leave some items behind!

notes.title: Latest in Cosmorists - May 2025
notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]

This is the month where the map was finally implemented into the game! There were a few bugs that I caught with it, such as the map UI unexpectedly crashing the game in rare instances.

[h1]Uploading the game's OST[/h1]
[list]
Although this isn't as related to the game itself, I've decided to upload the game's soundtrack to my YouTube channel after a long time without any videos, with one track being uploaded per day with the goal of eventually uploading all tracks currently available in the game! It's likely that the month of June will have at one video uploaded every day on the YouTube channel in the form of the game's soundtrack given that there are 38 tracks currently in use, as well as 11 more that are now either unused or only accessible in old saves.
[previewyoutube=dgRfMWjoApQ;full][/previewyoutube]
[/list]

[h1]Progress made so far[/h1]
[list]
This was mostly the month of implementing maps into the game alongside other changes. Those other changes weren't nearly tracked as well as prior updates, hence, a fairly small changelog for 0.1.4.
[/list]

[h1]Potential future plans[/h1]
[list]
Now that the map is mostly out of the way, I'm finally able to add some much needed content to the game!

Some content I will most likely prioritize are gadgets from certain biomes that provide a boost to a certain stat that doesn't have much of a boost yet, or provide special abilities, with the more advanced ones requiring electricity to function, which will most likely be found in treasure chests throughout various chests in differing biomes.

For late game content, I've considered utilizing the player's electricity beyond just gadgets providing certain abilities, where certain weapons consume the player's electricity from the fuel chamber to function, similar to the mana bar in other games like it, but is technology themed instead of magic themed.

In terms of Steam Deck support, that has also been highly, but it's likely going to be one of those major challenges to overcome and mainly be on the backburner. Its like how implementing a map into the game took a while, and it's very likely for this to also take a while, but will be worthwhile in the long run!

Due to the relatively slow pace of content in the past few months compared to most of 2024, and a simultaneous desire to add content to areas that lack it, I'm now likely to change my update plans. Updates in the 0.x or 0.x.y category are now less likely to be purely focused on one area. A main theme will still take hold, but it's now likely to add or make changes to other parts of the game that don't relate to the main theme.

I won't make any promises, as June still has the potential to be a slow month apart from uploading the game's soundtrack one video at a time every day, but with this new plan, there might just be a higher chance for content to come more densely than in the past few months. I may not get everything done, but possibly more than in past months!
[/list]

That's mostly what it was like for this month. Again, these future plans aren't a guarantee, but the less enjoyable part of game development, which was implementing a map, is now mostly out of the way. Steam Deck support is still considered, but is likely to be another less enjoyable aspect of game development that'll take longer to implement. For the most part, I'm eager to add content soon, even if it doesn't focus a specific theme as sharply as before!

notes.title: Latest in Cosmorists - Apr 2025
notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!

I've largely been busy outside of game development lately, causing the relative lack of updates. Progress however is still being made, especially within maps!

Right after my break, I focused on replacing the current way the game stores data with the new data structure, where I named it as an "object dictionary tree". Instead of carefully saving all the data in the form of byte arrays each time, the game will instead store all data in this data structure, and read from it when loading. I replaced all the saving code with this new way of saving. All the loading code only still remains for existing saves.

This is the month where the refactor was done, and it works for both new and existing saves at this point!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/24937ae3c065e113cf757aec8dbe24b87acbf009.png[/img]

This conversion is also the reason for the v 0.1.2 spaceship deletion bug, as the game now either deletes or overrides files that use the old format, one of which was spaceship data. The data was deleted, but wasn't replaced by the file that was supposed to override it when saved.

[list]
[previewyoutube=o7dWwaq8SJw;full][/previewyoutube]
This video above shows off the permafrost tools added in v 0.1.2, and is the first time I've done narration on the channel. The narration however is AI generated, and wanted to disclose its use. This is to experiment with something new on the channel surrounding the game after over a year of posting videos whose format barely changed apart from the trailers, which is mostly videos with text that show off something new added to the game with the soundtrack in the background.
It may not be the best quality for now, but it's definitely a start, and I'm likely going to experiment with the narration going forward!

[b]The game itself[/b]
[list]
In this case, I don't plan on using AI generated assets for use in the game. I do however use ChatGPT or other LLMs to generate a few ideas here and there, such as what some of the cave plants look like, refine those ideas to better suit the game, and implement them myself, and have been doing that on and off since early 2024.
[/list]

[b]The YouTube channel[/b]
[list]
The YouTube channel is likely going to contain many videos where at least one part of it is AI generated, with credits in the description as to which AI model was used. This is the primary area where I'll experiment with AI.
[/list]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[h1]What I'm working on[/h1]
[list]
Beyond the technical things, I'm currently attempting to add a map into the game.
[h3]Current navigational design[/h3]
[list]
The game is already designed around the lack of navigational options in the early game, where the lack of a map and the navigational cooldowns heavily incentivizes the player to obtain an item that can show players their way home more conveniently. Once players obtain a Bronze Compass, it also shows the way to the broken spaceship, which is how the game nudges new players into finding the spaceship without directly telling them apart from the "Lost? Press C" message.
[/list]
[h3]Where maps could belong[/h3]
[list]
At the moment, I'm considering making the map accessible right after the player repairs the spaceship, where it appears on the top-right corner of the screen, and will finally make the bronze compass less incentivized once repaired.
[/list]
[h3]Main technical challenges of maps[/h3]
[list]
The game technically already has a map in the form of landing sites for all worlds, but the map that I envision is one that also shows tiles the player has placed, such as houses, as well as each chunk having a different brightness level depending on the brightness of the explored chunk, which the landing site map doesn't do.
One challenge I have at the moment is how to make it run smoothly. These maps usually have to show 10s of thousands of tiles as single colors when zoomed out far enough, and iterating each of them to draw onto the screen every frame will lower the frame rate significantly when opened. That will be an optimization challenge to overcome at the moment.
As with many things in programming that involve large projects like this one, spaghetti code will be written at some point, which can often make it harder to implement new features, but there are other parts of the game's code organized enough to make adding new features fairly easy. For maps, it'll involve displaying world chunks, and the code responsible for dealing with world chunks is on the spaghetti end of the spectrum. Adding a map means mingling with world chunk code, which is likely to break or bug out other parts of the game that use world chunks.
[/list]
[h3]More biome-based updates[/h3]
[list]
Adding maps that I envision will be more difficult, but adding content to existing biomes is much easier to do in the current codebase, so it's likely for more biome-based updates to be rolled out in the future as I figure out how to add maps.
[/list]
[/list]

notes.title: Latest in Cosmorists - Jan 2025
notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!

2025 started off with the Narrow Echoes update with many changes! Following that was a more focused Verdant update that added a new cave biome a little over a week later! Let's get into the devlog!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[list]
Although Narrow Echoes was a fairly large update, the update was mostly all over the place in terms of what the game added or changed. Things such as graphical changes, quality of life improvements, steam achievements, steam cloud, autosaves, explosives, nighttime enemies, many ambient sounds and sound effects, and so on. Future updates are now going to have a different structure.
[/list]
[h1]The structure of future updates[/h1]
[list]
[h2]0.x updates[/h2]
[list]
These will still serve as the game's major updates, and are expected to take roughly the same amount of time to make of a few months. This time, it'll follow a particular theme. Instead of small / moderate changes spread out across the whole game like with Narrow Echoes, it'll focus on a broad yet specific part of the game that follows the main theme of the update.
One example is Aquatica. This is a whole planet, a fairly broad part of the game given that it has multiple biomes, many creatures, and unique resources, but is also one specific part of the game, as Aquatica is just one explorable world of 3 in the game so far.
In this example, it's a major update that focuses almost purely on Aquatica developed in the same time period as Narrow Echoes. The amount of content added to the game remains the same, but is much more concentrated.
It's also likely to touch other unrelated parts of the game, especially polishing up the game, but to a lesser degree, and the main purpose of those unrelated changes is to make the update feel a little bigger.
While these major updates are being made, it's likely for me to want to update another part of the game, and in that case, a regular update unrelated to the main theme is likely to be made in between to keep content flowing in these quieter periods of updates.
[/list]

For the less focused ones, it can be a new enemy in one biome, a new resource dropped by a new tile on another planet, and so on in one update, somewhat like a scaled down Narrow Echoes.
[/list]
[h2]0.x.y.z updates[/h2]
[list]
These updates are mostly unchanged, and they'll still serve as small bug-fixing / tweaking updates, not following a particular theme like the content updates. These will likely to be all over the place if it fixes many bugs that are in different unrelated parts of the game.
[/list]
[h2]Reasons for the structure change[/h2]
[list]
The primary reason for the structure change is for the updates to be more focused instead of being mostly spread out in many different parts of the game.

Immediately after fixing cloud bugs in v 0.1.0.2, almost all of my creative energy was directed at the Verdant caves, and apart from minor tweaks elsewhere, that was where all efforts went. This made the Verdant update (v 0.1.1) feel like a decently sized update after only a little over a week of working on it.

A major update with a more narrow focus made in a few months invested into the update's theme means a single thing to look forward to, and a lot more concentrated content for that theme!
[/list]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/d5472fb2ce1a458640b8d39ef56276c6865bd070.png[/img]
[h1]A programming tangent[/h1]
[list]
At the moment, my attention is focused on the way the game saves data. It's a bit of a mess, and felt that it needed a refactor.

[h2]How game data is stored[/h2]
[list]
Cosmorists is programmed in C#, but the same principle can apply to other programming languages.

Everything in the game is stored in raw binary, and mostly optimized for minimal storage usage. The type [i]int[/i] for instance, is often stored with a variable length.

[h3]An example of storing an integer[/h3]
[list]
Let's try the number 81000 as an example. It will save as a binary array like this: [03 68 3C 01] (These are hex numbers). The first byte, 03, tells the reader to look at the next 3 bytes: [68 3C 01]. The position of each byte is multiplied by a power of 256, and that power is equal to the index of the array.
Converting these to decimal values for familiarity, we get [104, 60, 1].
Conversion goes like this:
104 * 256 ^ 0 +
60 * 256 ^ 1 +
1 * 256 ^ 2
= 81000
[/list]
It's stored this way instead of blocks of 4 bytes mainly to reduce the amount of space smaller integers take up, and if for some reason, A [i]long[/i] should be used instead of an [i]int[/i], there's the added flexibility of being type-independent, as long as it's an integer being read.
[h3]An example of storing floating point numbers[/h3]
[list]
Floating point numbers are more precise values than integers, such as the player's position, the enemy's position, the temperature, the time of day, and other precise values.
In C#, there are [i]float[/i] and [i]double[/i] values. [i]float[/i] has less precision, and takes up 4 bytes. [i]double[/i] has more precision, but takes up 8 bytes.
These values are saved exactly as 4 or 8 byte chunks depending on the type.
[/list]
[/list]
I won't get into everything, but this is the basis of how the game stores data. Nearly everything in the game able to be saved is stored as an integer index, and that index is what gets saved, often taking as little as 2 bytes each on the disk. This is mostly how the game's save file size remains so small, only crossing around 100 KB in size after many hours of playing on the same save.
[h2]Why the refactor[/h2]
[list]
Although the file size is small, if I ever need to create a new class containing data that needs to be saved, I will always have to write code responsible for converting the data to a byte array, and more that reads from that byte array to get it to work with the disk.
There are also some classes who saving code is harder to modify when taking backwards compatibility into consideration, and if at some point, wish to add more data to a class that also needs to be saved, there will have to be if statements that checks the last version that was last played on so existing saves won't break, and after enough versions, that code can turn into a spaghetti mess that even I wouldn't understand well.
[/list]
[h2]The solution I'm aiming for[/h2]
[list]
3 Words. Key-Value pairs. This is where the game's saving code has long trended towards, and it works like this: The game saves a byte, and associates it with another piece of data, and that piece of data can have its own set of key-value pairs, going all the way down to either integers, or floating-point numbers.
Right after releasing the Verdant Update, I coded a more general-purpose data structure that stores data exclusively as key-value pairs, and it can also store instances of itself. I don't know what to call it, but I'll name it an "object dictionary tree" since it's recursive and works like a tree, makes heavy use of dictionary lookups, and takes in many basic types of objects.

A good analogy is the way files and folders are stored on operating systems. A file has a name with data inside, and a folder can store named subfolders and other files inside. Those subfolders can store more subfolders and files, and so on until the subfolders contain either nothing, or exclusively files without any subfolders of its own.

It can convert to and from a byte array with a single call, and the object dictionary tree does all the heavy lifting doing the conversion. It still deals with saving data to and from raw binary, such as the variable length integers, and floating point numbers taking up 4 or 8 bytes.

Here's an example of it in code filled with random data for testing purposes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/31511a52a516145e7ba8f13eb2eac844ce0f549a.png[/img]
In this example, each key is the first value in square brackets, and the associated values hold the data. It can be an [i]int[/i], a [i]long[/i], a [i]string[/i], an array of those types, or even another dictionary, and have its own set of key-value pairs, which can also store data in the same way.
If you're wondering, this takes up 199 bytes, and these are some of the first few bytes :)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/07b09e897682dccbbea5bd09e54aab8019f293d9.png[/img]
This 199 length byte array can also convert back to the data shown above, with the only difference being that the empty dictionaries and arrays are ignored when converting.

This solution is sought after for a few major reasons: Greater flexibility, an easier time maintaining backwards compatibility, and each class having less responsibility than before.

Dealing with saves will soon be easier once the refactor is done. If there's more data that needs to be saved, all I need to do is add the necessary variables containing the data to the tree, and when reading from it, assign the same variable from where it is in the tree.
It's very likely that saves will take up more storage than before, roughly 2x as much, as the byte arrays also contain additional bytes that tell the reader which variable type is saved, when to do recursion, and when to read arrays, but the file sizes are already small, and will make little difference on the disk.
[/list]
That's enough technical jargon that most of you likely didn't understand, now onto the creations :)
[/list]

Hello Cosmorists!

A new cave biome was added, and is the main focus of this update! You might want to go to Tierra if you're on another world, visit the Temperate forest biome, and go to their caves to see the new biome! It'll generate on existing saves as well!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/86ec72af9d66f81946ff18bb6bab82a3fb0a4fef.png[/img]

Temperate forests, being the only surface biome with no cave biome of its own on Tierra prior to this update, now has one, the Verdant Cave biome! Plant life here runs rampant, and so do some enemies, but look at the potential scenery of this new plant-filled biome!

notes.title: Narrow Echoes update now live!
notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!

The first major update of 2025 is here, kicking off the perfect square year with the Narrow Echoes update! Let's get to what's been added!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/886b109a5bb2d6d6876d33b94b635ff362b285e2.png[/img]
[list]
[h2]Swaying trees[/h2]
[list]
Is the world feeling a bit static? It will now feel less so with the trees now reacting to the wind, which will occasionally drop their leaves, and those leaves will also blow in the wind! Check out those new tree animations :D

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/ad33ca0c19e4b5649e6ab62482ce04ab58028b19.gif[/img]

[/list]
[h2]Much smaller worlds![/h2]
[list]
Exploring the world, only to encounter the same biome for millions of tiles? That will now change with worlds being much smaller for newer saves!

Exploring the world will now result in the same biome for a few thousand tiles instead of millions, which will allow exploring biomes once separated by thousands of kilometers much more manageable on foot!

There's also a new slider for small, medium, and large world sizes!
[/list]
[h2]Explosives[/h2]
[list]
Tired of mining one tile at a time with your pickaxe? This update offers a way to quickly destroy multiple tiles simultaneously!

Explosives!

So far, they're only found in treasure chests and barrels in caves, and are great for quickly mining large nodes of ore, but be careful, as they deal lots of damage if you're particularly close to the epicenter of any explosion they produce!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/7682366386d4487719ce9517e79c22310745cfc1.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h2]Research Stalkers[/h2]
[list]
The night on Tierra is about to offer a greater challenge to your scientific ambitions! Research Stalkers are creatures that don't care about any cosmorist wandering by. Their passive behavior will change dramatically as soon as it notices that your inventory contains science, where it will stalk you with a passion, trying to rob you of your scientific progress!

Once it steals your science, it will run away with your stolen science in an attempt to despawn, and once it despawns, so would the stolen science!

Here's how those research stalkers will behave once it tries to steal your science!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/45e02401646d5f3cf00935e8160d031e60bf18e9.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h2]Quick Stack[/h2]
[list]
A neat quality of life feature that wasn't initially announced is present in this update!
This feature allows players to move many of the same types of items to and from chests with the click of a single button!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/59bce12e777ef33245d0efe3c597a450319cb561.gif[/img]
[/list]
[h2]Other notable changes[/h2]
[list]
[h3]Steam cloud[/h3]
[list]
This is a feature that wasn't mentioned prior to the launch of the update, but the game now supports cloud saves! If you look at the saves menu, there will now be a cloud icon next to each of them indicating if they're on the Steam cloud. Existing saves won't be uploaded to the cloud when the game starts, but new saves will be uploaded by default. That behavior can be turned off in the settings, or for each individual save!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/8ab75d99ffc0a8289cc4462daf0475f1618b7d11.png[/img]
[/list]
[h3]Autosave[/h3]
[list]
Another feature relating to saves! The game will now automatically save every 10 minutes with a warning at the top of the screen when the game is about to autosave. This feature was added so that in the event of a game crash or freeze mid-session, less progress would be lost. The save interval can be changed in the settings, or can be turned off!
[/list]
[h3]No music at night on Tierra![/h3]
[list]
The music that used to play at night will no longer play, as the night in this update is more unsettling than in prior versions as the music would suggest. In its place are the idle sounds coming from the new enemies, and the ambient sounds!
If music is playing while the sun slowly sets, it'll fade out as usual, but after that, silence! The lack of music at night is intended to put more emphasis on the idle sounds of the new enemies! The section is added there in case this is reported as a bug :)
[/list]
[h3]And many more![/h3]
[list]
I could go on, but this list will get too long, now onto to the notable rebalances!
[/list]
[/list]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6ab5bce87a3b6dec5710952e67dc15a9989890ea.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/bfe63199e4876b4a3b9a31251a9d1bdff3d0d23a.png[/img]
[list]
[h1]Chemical Science[/h1]
[list]
Prior to this update, Chemical science was easier to obtain than Material science in the early game, but that's going to change!

Chemical Crystals[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/dc7123bb471556d13c9d45b2531be689576b6746.png[/img], the resource used as a part of the crafting recipe for Chemical science, is now harder to obtain in the early game, no longer spawning in the dirt caves. The only way to obtain it prior to discovering the chemical crystal biome is to kill some research stalkers, which has a 10% chance to drop a Chemical Crystal. This is meant to incentivize early game players to engage with the night to obtain the Chemical Crystals necessary to make Chemical Science!
[/list]
[h1]Magtise items now less common[/h1]
[list]
[h3]Ore generation[/h3]
[list]
Magtise ores are now twice as uncommon. It also has a chance to not generate if the temperature it's generated at is between 40°C and 100°C, where lower temperatures in this range further increases the ore's rarity.
[/list]
[h3]Treasure[/h3]
[list]
Treasures in the lava caves will no longer contain magtise tools or weapons, with the only magtise item able to be generated now being magtise spears.
[/list]
[h3]Enemies[/h3]

All enemies in the lava caves except for the Magtise wanderer will no longer drop Magtise ore.
Magtise wanderers also spawn 4x less frequently, drop 2x less Magtise ore, and will no longer spawn if the ambient temperature is less than 50°C.
[/list]
[h3]Intended effect[/h3]
[list]
Removing all of these options to obtain Magtise ore makes mining it, or fighting Magtise wanderers the best way to obtain it. The deeper the player goes, the more common it gets, but also the more common dangerous enemies are, and the hotter it gets.
This is also intended to increase the value of finding Magtise ore, and the excitement for crafting tools and weapons out of it!

[list]

[previewyoutube=rLYrkoAP3Ak;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]New logo[/h1]
[list]
If you saw the new trailer, you might have noticed that the logo looks different from the current one. That's because in the upcoming update, the logo is going to change to the new one without the "Narrow Echoes" strip, and will also replace the one in-game!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/d211df61e1781751956387639ec14e926ed95709.png[/img]
[h3]Why the logo is changing[/h3]
[list]
[b]Back to June 2023[/b]
[list]
Lets go back to June 2023. This was before the game had science, before it had automation, before it even had multiple planets to explore, although the ability to do so was actively being worked on at the time. There was a lot less certainty as to what kind of game Cosmorists would evolve into back then.

[list]

[h1]Much smaller planets[/h1]
[list]
In the current version, planet sizes are comparable to Earth in real life, and it remained this way since alpha 0.20 from January 2024. As I played the game however, I gradually came to the conclusion that making planets this large was likely not the best move for Cosmorists. As you explore the world from the spawn point on Tierra, the only new things to discover for thousands of kilometers on the surface are a few new plant types and food, a grassy biome, and that would be it, repeating across millions of tiles. notes.content:
Hello Cosmorists!

Last week, v 0.0.1 was released, and since then, I added a little more content in this update than the last, as well as some more technical changes to try and reduce the frequency of crash reports. Now let's get to the content added for this update!

[h2]Burner drills![/h2]
[list]
Itching to mine that ground ore, but you can't due to electric drills and automation tech being buried too deep in the tech tree? We'll does this update offer a possible solution...

Burner drills!

A primitive form of early game automation able to be unlocked in the tech tree after assemblers, and just before unlocking electrical science! They're slower than their electrical counterparts, but can be useful in accumulating a small amount of ore before jumping into electrical technologies!

[h1]Main highlights of this update[/h1]
[list]

[list]
[h3]Local variations[/h3]
The temperature system now has a few new features. Furnaces will now heat up the player's surroundings depending on the type of furnace, and a method to cool your surroundings down in the early game was added as well!

Here's the evaporative cooler in action in a desert, a hot biome. It cools down the player's surroundings with liquid water, and the effects are greater the closer the player is to the evaporative coolers!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/49192b4f7d27d89a70fa3cc0aacaa93867e1c54a.gif[/img]

[h3]Diurnal variations on Tierra[/h3]
Different biomes will now have different variations in their day and night temperatures. Most rocky fields and deserts will have a higher temperature variation of around 15-20°C (Very rarely up to a 30°C difference), while more forested biomes such as Taigas, Temperate Forests, and Jungles will have lower variations, usually less than a 10°C difference.

[h3]Diurnal variations on Luna[/h3]
Due to the lack of an atmosphere, the temperature difference between day and night are now much greater, usually having more than a 200°C difference between day and night. Temperatures on Luna will still have no impact on the player's survival.

[h3]Diurnal variations on Aquatica[/h3]
Since this is an oceanic planet, the variations here are now much lower, usually less than a 3°C difference between day and night regardless of biome. Speaking of Aquatica...
[/list]

[h2]Optimizations[/h2]
[list]
Optimized the tile renderer to run more smoothly in most cases. The GPU will now do most of the work, and the CPU sends tile data to the GPU only when the player moves to a new chunk. In older versions, the CPU does most of the heavy lifting on a single core for every tile every frame, leading to low frame rates when zoomed out far enough where thousands of tiles have to be rendered.
[/list]

[list]
[*] All particles now move in 3D space, where particles appear larger the closer it is to the camera in the z axis.
[*] Particles will now have a buoyancy effect. It's especially apparent on Aquatica where text will now rise to float above the water.
[*] Reduced how long damage numbers and bouncy text linger after appearing.
[/list]

[list]
[*] Doubled the rate of oxygen consumption on Luna and Aquatica.
[/list]
[h2]Treasure[/h2]
[list]
[*] Increased the quantity of the majority of treasure items by a factor of 2 or 3, and doubled the coin cost of all the treasure.
[/list]
[h2]UI[/h2]
[list]
[*] A new sound effect is now played when scrolling in the main menu UI.
[*] Items will now show more descriptions when hovered on, and they all use the same font as the text displaying the name of the item.
[/list]
[/list]
[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where deep in the caves of all planets, around a few thousand layers deep, the temperature jumps suddenly.
[/list]

In the future, it's likely that the initial spaceship will no longer go to space, and only be used to orbit Tierra. This would be intended to make the player explore other biomes for the resources needed to upgrade to the currently new spaceship, which can both orbit, and explore other planets.

notes.title: v alpha 0.22
notes.content:
It's been a little while since the previous update, and now it's finally out. It introduces automation, and for now, it's somewhat limited, but I plan to expand on the automation mechanic in the future, and make it the focus of the game at a certain point in the player's progression.

[h1]Main highlights of this update[/h1]
[h2]Automation[/h2]

The player can now automate placing items in and out of chests by using conveyor belts and inserters. Here it is in action when an inserter takes wood from a chest, and transports the wood via conveyor belt to another chest:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/9c621bc30ef8d341f4b441f2d79148ea3bc88642.gif[/img]

This update also adds ground ore patches that the player is unable to mine by any means, but [i]can[/i] be mined by electric powered drills. The drill however can only mine the ore at around 10 ore / hour for copper and tin, and 4 ore / hour for iron ore, even when fully powered. This slow rate is intended to put ore automation in the background while the player does something else, and make the transition from survival-crafting game to automation game more smooth. The ore can also be smelted via electric furnaces to automate ore smelting. Here it is in action:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/428b3b775281f0b11dea010bb04e94c31661bb61.gif[/img]
Those ground ore patches also have a finite amount of ore, and can eventually be used up by the drills. So far, the only ground ore patches in the game are copper, tin, and iron.

Those flashing icons indicate a low power supply, mostly caused by the furnace. The electric furnace also requires electricity to function, and it comes from the power grid.

[h2]Power grid[/h2]

Electric machines have been added to the game, where they need to be connected to a power source to transfer the electricity to the machine via electric poles. For now, there's only one type of electric pole.
Here's a power plant powering these carbon extractors, a new machine added to the game:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/2441f00d7e4478c4c67be72f185e8180edbe7b6c.png[/img]
Those power plants don't have animations yet, but will likely be added in the future to indicate activity.

notes.content:
[h1]Main highlights of this update[/h1]
[h2]Electricity[/h2]
The player can now store energy as electricity after unlocking a new Electricity technology using a new science!

Here's the new energy bar next to the health and hunger bars once the Electricity technology has been researched:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/bbb1b100c2e43591c0cbc008294d0b81d1bb390d.png[/img]

This update also introduces a new science: [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/49d7da57eb03c4fe3c73a4fdf0e67bd9dad84c50.png[/img] Electrical science, able to be researched after the Basic Assembler tech.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/0a2227bf9a0e1b842e0a3d5e168d2dc86c574a17.png[/img]

[h2]Enhancers[/h2]

This update also adds enhancers, which can't be accessed by the player until the Enhancer tech is researched. These are items that are intended to be put onto the player to help survive harsher environments.

The enhancers that have been added into this update are heaters and coolers, and when placed into the enhancer slot, the heater will warm up the player's surroundings when the ambient temperature is cold enough, and the cooler will cool down their surroundings when it's hot enough while consuming the player's stored electricity.
These can also be paired with cold and/or heat resistance buffs respectfully to enable the player to explore environments that would otherwise be out of reach for them.

Here's a screenshot of the UI for the new fuel chamber unlocked with the Electricity tech on the left, and the enhancers unlocked with the Enhancers tech on the right:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/51362eb281ddae3b957f5a1265aafe30b266260e.png[/img]

Here's a gif of when the player has energy generated with Oak Wood in the fuel chamber, while in a hot environment with a cooler kicking in. Notice the slower rate of power generation as the cooler becomes more active:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/d06d8410d39c7750b01aba8ae2b660f1afa2176f.gif[/img]

Here's a video diving into greater detail into both electricity and enhancers:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXuEyLTmKt8

This update also adds a new set of 3 related biomes to Matica, all of which are geometric biomes

Surface variant (Geometric surface):
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/0b33774448019ab38520e1e0adbc90efd9c5e43b.png[/img]

Cave variant (Geometric caves):
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/c8d501c99009c6629ac846672be5c5ce15be0221.png[/img]

The 3rd variant (Lush Geometry):
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/adb89fa56a289d5986a3b452d5b22c8fddc0fbde.png[/img]

It's a biome that's mostly focused on using geometric shapes as resources, like how integers are resources on Matica. This biome will wrap around the equator and be the warmest biome on Matica for now, but it's still too cold for any player to survive in.

Here's a video going into greater detail about this geometric biome, and a rough 10 minute playtest at the end:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PAINAhMrT7M

Note that updates that add new biomes will require a new save for backwards compatibility reasons.

notes.title: v alpha 0.20
notes.content:
[h1]The big three changes of this update[/h1]
[h2]Main menu[/h2]
This update kicks off with a much needed overhaul to some main menu UIs. The start of it looks mostly the same apart from the settings icon being gray instead of blue, but the UIs for many of them have been redesigned and polished with new space-y menu music playing in the background!

The world selection UI:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/b7dcc6900dca32d95a08618f5d61f989c78df59e.gif[/img]
This UI now has some sound effects when hovering over a save file, and when scrolling for some polish!

The audio UI:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/e11986977b8e96fa7876aada8b5b317f513ec518.png[/img]

The player controls UI:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/d1c3e86ed9bc257bd76ff602b9e17b458c0544bb.png[/img]

The display UI:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/fb11d1b127c3fd84c1cdc677fb841fb9eddee120.png[/img]
Notice that there are now settings for going fullscreen, and the resolution when going fullscreen. These are features taken for granted in other games regardless of the genre, but were completely absent from Cosmorists until this update!

[h2]Landing sites[/h2]
The player now has the option to land anywhere on the planet via landing sites instead of a single landing spot. Each landing site will tell the player what biome it is, what the temperature is, and the coordinates of the landing site. Since each landing site is 1049 km across, or 2²⁰ tiles across and each site is a similar distance apart from each other, it reveals the millions of square kilometers of explorable land to explore!
This is the player landing on a different part of Tierra as seen in the gif below: 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/32cdeb412787557bcc173cc64a16d3b3e7e58009.gif[/img]
Note that the appearance of the map above will only apply to saves created in this update. Existing saves will still have this feature, but the map for those existing saves will look more like what's seen in the image below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/bb75e715bfb8f4049e19f606cac24664b9b85859.png[/img]
[b]Why does the map for existing saves look all jumbled?[/b]
This is to make existing saves backwards compatible with the new update. If this new world generation overrides the existing saves, the player's main base will suddenly be in a hot desert, savanna, subtropical forest, or jungle biome, with temperatures suddenly jumping to between 35°C in the best case scenario and 65°C in the worst case. Keeping the map this way will ensure that a scenario like this never occurs. This isn't a bug, it's the old generation system at work, but zoomed out so far that it looks like a random, disorganized mess of biomes.

For the saves created in this update, here's what to expect from this video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7V1Y4c4OE2k
For the initial introduction that evolved into the map in the video above, here's what it was like here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6-KsN4NWBco

After the spaceship is repaired, the player is able to go into orbit with less fuel required to take off than going to another planet, but will only allow the player to land somewhere else on the planet. In the screenshot below, the player can't go to another planet due to the weight, but can still afford to orbit.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/5d4ea20d88f8a47f288d406db741bbf4a7f1966f.png[/img]
Once in orbit, a map will automatically appear asking where on the planet to land.

[h2]Treasure[/h2]
This update also adds treasure. They can be scattered around occasionally on the surface in the form of crates, but are most common in caves of all worlds except for Luna. All treasure will cost coins to open, which simultaneously adds the first incentive for players to obtain coins via enemies, encouraging combat, and reduces the game loop's dependency on mining. This gives combat a larger role for obtaining resources both directly from the enemy, and coins to save up for treasure.

Here's a sample of treasure found on the surface for a cheap price of around 4 coins per crate in the gif below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/da245a395c9b30b8413eaf0b971f3a1d576031cb.gif[/img]

Here's a demonstration of the player opening up more expensive treasure in the caves in the gif below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/483b8e1c6ae8a78f1d771ce6339846d555ce3a05.gif[/img]

They can also spawn in other planets, this is barrel treasure in Aquatica's caves:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/d3effb8b8068eb7461deba918271a9b54d6a7cc6.gif[/img]

For more details on this treasure system, here it is in the video below:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X46p_SSFBFg



[h1]Other highlights[/h1]
[h2]Doors[/h2]
In the world of base building, one thing was missing, and that was doors. They've been added in this update as well, and the player's base will now be safer from enemies without having to break and place walls each time the player wants to enter or leave their base!

Here's the door in action from this gif:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/b5dfc3693cf5e9efbeeccbb8f3ca67c0cc85597e.gif[/img]

[h2]Player[/h2]
When mining something by hand, the player will now have a mining animation as seen in the gif below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/a5c7b575cc115fb2aa3ede4a483bfde496d45454.gif[/img]
In that gif is coal ore, a new ore intended to be used as an alternative fuel source for furnaces and spaceships.

[h2]World Generation[/h2]
[h3]All worlds[/h3]
The biomes of all new saves will now span hundreds, sometimes over 1000 km across. The only exception to this are sub-biomes, most commonly in caves, whose size is similar to that of the old world generation.
[h3]Tierra[/h3]
In the dirt, mushroom, and berry caves, dirt walls will now generate alongside stone as a cave wall with less durability than the stone ones, making it easier to dig through for lower tier pickaxes.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/621d017c21601507808f60ae38a5c7822306f03b.png[/img]



[h1]Smaller changes[/h1]
[h2]Ambience[/h2]
+ Ambience for swamp and jungle caves.
[h2]Crafting[/h2]
+ (Stone(8), Iron Bar(1), -1 Integer(1)) --> Iron Cave Entrance(1)
+ (Bronze Bar(1/4), Gold Bar(1), -3 Integer(1)) --> Gold Cave Entrance(1)
- Magtise crafting on Luna
[h2]Items[/h2]
[b]19 new items[/b]

notes.title: v alpha 0.19
notes.content:
[h1]Highlights of this update[/h1]
[h2]An overhauled smelting system[/h2]
The new smelting system includes a new UI for it, and all ores will now require time and fuel to convert ores into their respective bars. I also removed the one-click recipes needed to smelt them into 1/4 bar for this new system. Here's a demonstration of this new system in action:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/cdf0f9e1a163380b56e4db7ccd707496d4afc8b5.png[/img] With copper ore:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/7d1e65f0c2f6debb3423bbaafbb2399be400bf5f.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/cdf0f9e1a163380b56e4db7ccd707496d4afc8b5.png[/img] With tin ore:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/28a1b591662b052ba8f93c76014db5ff186c8016.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/677f999d1f7697c9d831551178eb3568538b316f.png[/img](2x speed with bronze furnace) With copper ore:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/a68764e2199d79606d9ec82a3aff3dc73afae194.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/677f999d1f7697c9d831551178eb3568538b316f.png[/img] With iron ore:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/94a89dc9173d68bbbb58ecf33a65ad25e4b5cca1.gif[/img]

If the player has unlocked the associated tech in the tech tree, there will be a little upgrade icon showing that an upgrade is possible. If the player can afford it, it'll show as green, otherwise, it'll be red. Once clicked on, the stone furnace will upgrade to a bronze furnace. Here's a demo showing what happens when upgraded:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/08ef8f9914c11a5cc7c3680c28a6c8bf075e1d33.gif[/img]
A YouTube video diving deeper into this new smelting system, and my plans to eventually add automation into the late-stages of the game:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vekHsc_yQnQ&pp=ygUKY29zbW9yaXN0cw%3D%3D

[h2]Glowing enemies[/h2]
Certain enemies in the game can now glow in the dark. Lava slimes are one example, and here's a dim screenshot of them in the lava caves of Tierra in a dark area attacking the player:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/5f833a8ebefea049d62e5af331764bcdef59ea3a.png[/img]
The same thing goes for anglerfish in the deep seas of Aquatica, but the lights they emit are brighter and more concentrated than the ones that lava slimes emit. Here's another screenshot of three of them in the dark:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/4694ac24f968a7aaa834aa59f8ff7e3b1ac03c55.png[/img]
A YouTube video showing footage of the glowing enemies, and their actions:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ftK1HjoLrFU&pp=ygUKY29zbW9yaXN0cw%3D%3D

[h1]Crafting[/h1]
- (1 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/b9bfc1df660fc499b4a63876122b6fcfe993db3f.png[/img] + 3 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6614d8599c4eb379c65683800ea89e4955e195a7.png[/img] -> 1 1/2 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/16e891036d9150d1966d4d6f382f5c2548ea2163.png[/img]) removed, as there's no way to get [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/6614d8599c4eb379c65683800ea89e4955e195a7.png[/img] nitrogen.

[h1]Enemies[/h1]
+ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/2e40b4fe0ff1646d93edcb778f8b462fd5b05133.png[/img] Multiplication vomiter (Matica)
+ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/01c6901f760f69c36306cd9bd451d2ab9a61b9a6.gif[/img] Lanternfish (Aquatica)
[h2]Other[/h2]
~ Certain hostile enemies will now behave differently depending on whether they can see the player or not.
~ Removed the stone drop from all enemies except stone-based ones such as ore critters and rock slimes.

[h1]Items[/h1]
+ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/12c8d05e42747e9ae14bee54a91638bc109c4478.png[/img]Iron Oxygenator
~ Decreased the mass of all wood types except [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/2250a9b7a84cdf9a1b9ad2bdd245ab989a731271.png[/img]Cherry Blossom wood from 600g to 250g.
~ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/628bcbbf3569c7a6208bd4a31739338951e547a0.png[/img]Bamboo wood, can now be used as fuel. Provides 2 fuel each.
~ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/2250a9b7a84cdf9a1b9ad2bdd245ab989a731271.png[/img]Cherry Blossom wood, decreased mass from 800g to 300g.
~ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/61b69236a99859fba1c759af25611ffa8fd1c145.png[/img]Crude Oil, decreased max stack size from 5040 to 840, increased fuel value from 6 to 10, and decreased the mass from 1kg to 300g.
~ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/b13c64f212504cbbd2d45cb063c1ef24c74b33b6.png[/img]Crystalline Oxygen, increased oxygen heal from 3 to 8.
~ [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/2f6f7ebebdd1bb0e942526d6f639a7061a01b6ef.png[/img]Plant matter, increased the mass from 3g to 20g each, and decreased the fuel value from 0.5 to 0.05 each. This nerf is intended to incentivize other fuels.

[h1]Player[/h1]
~ Temperature transfer rate on oceanic worlds like Aquatica is now constant for all pressures.

[h1]Quality of life[/h1]
~ On top of the ctrl moving feature, Left-Shift clicking on an item in the inventory while a chest is opened will cause only that item stack to get transferred instead of all identical items in left-ctrl.
The feature in action using the left-shift key only:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/784ace1a99e45af7ffe36b664fe26eb977c0ace3.gif[/img]
+ Left-Shift + left click on a nearby furnace will automatically transfer the output items to the inventory.
The feature in action. When the bronze bars disappear, the Left-Shift key was held, and clicked the left mouse button:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/33b92fcafb012634f550f28f39bf5f2324cc66f2.gif[/img]

[h1]Sound effects[/h1]
+ Upgrade spaceship sound effect
+ Upgrade furnace sound effect

[h1]Spaceships[/h1]
~ Changed how spaceships convert items into fuel. The old system calculates the time needed to convert based on how much fuel each item provides to the 2/3 power, and halved. E.g. Crude oil provided 6 fuel each, and it takes 0.5*6^(2/3) seconds, or 1.56 seconds to convert one unit crude oil into 6 fuel. This new system is now based on mass, and each spaceship converts mass into fuel per second, and the default one, and the only one in the game so far, converts items into fuel at a rate of 0.5kg/s. With crude oil providing 10 fuel each in this update, and weighing 0.3kg, it'll now take 0.3kg/(0.5kg/s), or 0.6 seconds to convert one unit of crude oil into fuel.

[h1]Tech tree[/h1]
~ Researching certain technologies will now require the player to obtain an item before it can be researched. E.g. Gold smelting now requires the player to obtain gold ore for the first time in the playthrough before it can be unlocked. This is intended to prevent spoiling late-game content for new players.

[h1]World Generation[/h1]
[list]
[h2]All worlds[/h2]
[*] Tiles such as stones, trees, and any tile with variants will now generate in a more shuffled manner.
[h2]Aquatica[/h2]
[*] Doubled the spawn rate of copper and tin ore.
[*] Players will now spawn in areas between 25°C and 30°C to prevent the onset of hypothermia in the default spawning area.
[*] There's a chance for players to spawn in coral reefs due to this change in the temperature spawning point.
[h2]Luna[/h2]
[*] Titanium ore is now 5x less common. This is intended to incentivize players to risk Aquatica's deep sea, and crushing pressures for a steady source of Titanium.
[h2]Matica[/h2]
[*] Tripled the spawn rate of crystalline oxygen.
[h2]Tierra[/h2]
[*] Increased the spawn rate of iron ore between layers 12-100 for most biomes, and for the stone cave one.
[*] Copper, tin, and iron ore can now spawn in ice caves.
[/list]

[h1]Bug fixes[/h1]
[list]
[h2]Large bugs[/h2]
[*] Sliding against a wall will almost always cause the player to get stuck on the tile ahead of it.
[*] The player is unable to go through gaps that are one tile (1m) wide.
[*] Players will often get stuck inside solid tiles when the framerate is low, or is moving at high speeds.
[*] Loading the game in a save that's saved in a cave will cause the cave entrances to not show up in the compass.
[*] Loading old saves with spaceship fuel available to convert can sometimes cause the game to freeze completely when clicked on.
[h2]Medium bugs[/h2]
[*] The spaceship doesn't convert items into fuel when the player is in the caves.
[h2]Small bugs[/h2]
[*] Left ctrl or shift clicking on an item in the inventory with another will often cause the item to go after the nearest empty slot instead of the nearest slot with that item.
[*] Enemies that spawn in the dark caves of Tierra will start spawning in layer 96 (960m) instead of layer 100 (1km)
[/list]

Some players report that the game is crashing when they try to boot it. Older versions were dependent on the .NET framework, making the game more susceptible to technical issues and crashes. This build of the game is now somewhat larger in file size, but it's self contained, and no longer needs an external .NET framework to run. I'm unsure if this completely solves most of technical issues, but it seems less likely to pop up again for anything relating to external .NET framework dependencies, and any technical issues would hopefully be caused by the game's code itself, and not anything external.

On the store page, The minimum disk space requirement has doubled from Minimum 200 MB, Recommended 250 MB to 400 MB and 500 MB respectively to account for the gradual increase in download size as I keep updating the game.

From this point forward, all future versions of Cosmorists will be self contained to avoid the requirement of needing to download the right .NET framework at a cost of a few 10s of megabytes on your hard drive.

[h3]What I might do with this in the future:[/h3]
I do plan to add more tiles like this where it takes the player's health, such as poisonous tiles in the swamp/jungles, liquid nitrogen if I ever add in a planet cold enough to harbor it, and possibly pointy tiles.

notes.title: A new world creation UI
notes.content:
I added in new UI for world creation and can finally name saves upon creation instead of names like "World0", "World1", "World2", as well as providing an optional integer seed value.

Before this, saves were named by the game starting with World0, then World1, World2, World3 depending on the availability of the smallest available numeric suffix. The only way you could name your saves is by closing the game, going to the saves folder, renaming the folder, and relaunching the game.

Now naming saves is possible in-game, as well as the ability to optionally provide an integer seed value for world generation of each planet so that it's possible for seeds to be shared with other people for any cool things the world generation algorithm ends up churning up!

notes.title: Water pressure vs your health!
notes.content:
I now made it to where the deeper underwater you go, the less max health you have due to the water pressure. The more water pressure there is when your cosmorist is unprepared, the less max health there is available. So far, there's no way to increase pressure tolerance or reducing the negative effects on your cosmorist, but I plan to add it in the tech tree at some point in the future!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/4fd756879f97ae13135b461e3e76346681fb9384.png[/img]
The image above features the starting area of the twilight ocean biome with 13 atmospheres of water pressure. The max HP is now 90 HP instead of the usual 120 HP for a starter cosmorist.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/91cb6c75098e851d23d3bc8b62e4dda2ec84c42f.png[/img]
The image above is the beginning of the deep sea biome under 120 atmospheres of pressure. Under normal circumstances, your cosmorist will be crushed within only a few hundred milliseconds and the max health is 19 HP.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/7571bc6e479a4c69849866534631bc59f8358497.png[/img]
The image above is the cosmorist under 238 atmospheres of pressure in the deep sea biome. The max health is 6 HP, low enough for most dangers to one shot a cosmorist!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44545324/3ebf4ff4bc6e1ee8d1249d7ab18ac173fbe0d9c8.png[/img]
The image above features my character in the deep sea biome under 712 atmospheres of water pressure. When visiting unprepared, this much pressure will crush your cosmorist in 1 frame. If your cosmorist is prepared except for the max health, it'll cap out at just 1 HP, easily low enough for any danger to one shot a cosmorist.
